record.context_brief: Index theorems from skew lattice coset structure
record.original_question: Determine whether index-theorem results can always be obtained from the coset structure of skew lattice varieties, as happens for some known varieties, and determine what such combinatorial results can contribute to the study of skew lattices.

evidence.quote: The index theorems presented for some varieties of skew lattices in [3, 17] and [19] show a combinatorial perspective
Can we always obtain such results? What can they bring to the study of skew lattices?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A skew lattice is an algebra $(S; \wedge, \vee)$ with two associative idempotent binary operations satisfying the absorption identities $x \wedge (x \vee y) = x = x \vee (x \wedge y)$ and $(x \wedge y) \vee y = y = (x \vee y) \wedge y$. On any skew lattice, Leech's natural preorder is defined by $x \preceq y$ iff $x \wedge y \wedge x = x$ and $y \vee x \vee y = y$, and the natural partial order is $x \leq y$ iff $x \wedge y = x = y \wedge x$ (equivalently $x \vee y = y = y \vee x$). Green's relation $\mathcal{D}$ is the congruence whose blocks are the maximal rectangular subalgebras; the quotient $S/\mathcal{D}$ is a (commutative) lattice. Given comparable $\mathcal{D}$-classes $A > B$, each element $b \in B$ determines cosets $A \wedge b \wedge A \subseteq A$ and $b \vee A \vee b \subseteq B$, and $A$ is partitioned into a disjoint union of $B$-cosets in $A$, all of the same cardinality; the index $[A:B]$ is defined as the number of such cosets. An "index theorem" for a variety $\mathcal{V}$ of skew lattices is a combinatorial identity (in the spirit of Lagrange-type theorems) relating the cardinalities and indices of $\mathcal{D}$-classes inside any finite member of $\mathcal{V}$, derived purely from its coset structure.

Problem: Determine whether, for every variety $\mathcal{V}$ of skew lattices, an index theorem can be obtained from the coset structure of the members of $\mathcal{V}$. If such results can be established, determine what combinatorial information about skew lattices in $\mathcal{V}$ they yield (e.g., regarding enumeration, structural decompositions, or invariants of finite skew lattices).
artifact.status_search_result: Index theorems are known for certain specific varieties of skew lattices (e.g., results by Pita Costa and others on coset laws and distributive/categorical skew lattices), but no general index-theorem result covering all varieties has appeared in the literature, and the question of what such combinatorial results contribute to the broader theory remains a stated open direction.

status_evidence.title: On the coset structure of a skew lattice
status_evidence.snippet: Develops coset structure for skew lattices and proves index/Lagrange-type results in specific cases.
status_evidence.claim: Index theorems are established only for certain classes of skew lattices via the coset structure.

status_evidence.title: Flat Coset Decompositions of Skew Lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies coset decompositions giving combinatorial information for particular subclasses.
status_evidence.claim: Combinatorial coset-based theorems exist for some varieties but not as a general result.

status_evidence.title: On the coset laws for skew lattices in rings
status_evidence.snippet: Coset laws derived for skew lattices arising in rings.
status_evidence.claim: Specific varieties admit coset-based combinatorial laws, suggesting a partial picture rather than a universal index theorem.
